Used a factor of one hundred rather than one thousand
Correct application of the principle

questions.explanation: During a phase change the temperature stays constant while energy goes into rearranging the structure, so Q equals mass times specific latent heat. Here 98 g times 236 J per g gives 23128 J, or 23.13 kJ after dividing by one thousand.

questions.stem: Trial 886000447: an ideal gas of carbon dioxide with 1.6 mol expands isothermally at 470 K from 1.3 L to 3.6 L; how much heat must be supplied, in kJ?

options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Halved the temperature in the nRT factor
Omitted the logarithm from the work expression
Altered the volume ratio by adding one to it

questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant temperature the internal energy does not change, so by the first law the heat supplied equals the work done by the gas, nRT ln(Vf over Vi). With the given volumes and temperature this is 6.44 kJ; heat must flow in to balance the expansion work.
questions.hint: At constant T for an ideal gas, Q = W = nRT ln(Vf/Vi).

Used gamma rather than gamma minus one as the exponent
Correct application of the principle
Inverted the initial-to-final volume ratio

questions.explanation: For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process T V raised to gamma minus one is constant, so Tf equals Ti times (Vi over Vf) to the power gamma minus one.
